rationale: Thyroid hormone and IL-6 comparison with healthy dogs; no treatment or outcome.

title: Platelet activation and platelet-leukocyte interaction in dogs naturally infected with Babesia rossi.
design: case-control flow cytometry study of natural infection
rationale: Abstract compares survivors and non-survivors but describes no treatment; no open full text was found.

title: Clinical babesiosis and molecular identification of Babesia canis and Babesia gibsoni infections in dogs from Serbia.
design: clinicopathological case series with molecular identification
rationale: All 60 dogs received imidocarb but no response, follow-up or outcome is reported.

title: Tick-borne Diseases (Borreliosis, Anaplasmosis, Babesiosis) in German and Austrian Dogs: Status quo and Review of Distribution, Transmission, Clinical Findings, Diagnostics and Prophylaxis.
design: multi-pathogen narrative review with prevalence maps
rationale: Multi-pathogen review of transmission, diagnosis and prophylaxis; treatment of clinical disease is not covered in the abstract.

title: Babesiosis.
journal: Revue scientifique et technique (International Office of Epizootics)
design: narrative review of canine babesiosis
rationale: Full text treatment section names imidocarb, diminazene, trypan blue, atovaquone-azithromycin and diminazene-imidocarb-clindamycin, and discusses prognosis, response and relapse.

title: Serum canine pancreatic-specific lipase concentrations in dogs with naturally occurring Babesia rossi infection.
journal: Journal of the South African Veterinary Association
design: prospective observational biomarker study of natural infection
rationale: Admission lipase concentrations and SIRS; no treatment or outcome reported.

title: Clinical, haematological, cytokine and acute phase protein changes during experimental Babesia gibsoni infection of beagle puppies.
design: experimental case-controlled longitudinal study
rationale: Experimental infection followed without treatment.

title: Serum levels of the chemokines keratinocyte chemoattractant and interleukin-8 in dogs naturally infected with Babesia canis canis
design: comparison of serum chemokines in infected vs healthy dogs
rationale: Chemokine concentrations compared by severity; no treatment described.

title: Razine kemokina KC i IL-8 u serumu pasa prirodno zaraženih vrstom Babesia canis canis.
design: case-control biomarker study of natural infection (chemokines vs severity)
rationale: Duplicate chemokine report with no abstract; the finding line shows biomarker comparison only, no treatment.

title: CLINICAL, HEMATOLOGICAL AND PARASITOLOGICAL STUDY ON CANINE BABESIOSIS
design: clinical, haematological and blood-film survey of dogs, infected vs healthy
rationale: Clinical and haematological survey; no treatment or outcome in the abstract.

title: Platelet indices in dogs with Babesia rossi infection.
design: observational platelet-index study with controls, by outcome
rationale: Platelet indices at 24 and 48 h in admitted survivors and 12 deaths are reported, but the treatment given is not described in abstract or note.
access_note: Full text not in data/markdown (abstract only); publisher page paywalled, not open access in Europe PMC.

title: Characteristics, immunological events, and diagnostics of Babesia spp. infection, with emphasis on Babesia canis
journal: Bulletin of the Veterinary Institute in Pulawy
design: narrative review of Babesia biology, immunity and diagnostics
rationale: Narrative review of biology, immunity and diagnostics; no treatment coverage.

title: Nitric oxide, protein oxidation and total antioxidant levels in serum of dogs naturally infected by Ehrlichia canis, Leishmania infantum and Babesia vogeli
design: case-control biomarker study of natural single and co-infections
species: B. vogeli (PCR), E. canis, L. infantum
rationale: Oxidative biomarkers in single and co-infections; no treatment or outcome.

title: Prognostic Markers in Acute Babesia canis Infections.
design: survivor vs nonsurvivor prognostic study; 3 experimental dogs
rationale: Full text: all naturally infected dogs received imidocarb (with doxycycline in some, second imidocarb dose at 14 days); 7 survived and were cured by smear and PCR at 14 days, 8 died or were euthanised.

title: Excessive Pro-Inflammatory Serum Cytokine Concentrations in Virulent Canine Babesiosis.

rationale: Full text Methods: dogs received standard care with diminazene 3.5 mg/kg, packed red cell transfusion and IV fluids as needed, and short-term survival was recorded (85 survived, 12 died). Changed from exclude under the rule.

title: Reliability of clinical monitoring for the diagnosis of babesiosis in dogs in Nigeria.
design: observational study of suspected cases, smear-positive vs smear-negative
rationale: Smear-positive dogs were treated mostly with oxytetracycline, with recovery and 7 deaths among 44 so treated; main aim is diagnostic reliability of clinical indices.

title: Clinical Management of Acute Renal Failure due to Babesiosis in a Dog
design: single-case clinical report of acute renal failure in babesiosis
rationale: Single dog with acute renal failure managed with aggressive fluid therapy and antiprotozoal chemotherapy, reported as successful.

title: Septic shock - similarities and differences of postmortem findings in canine babesiosis and leptospirosis
design: post-mortem and histopathology comparison, babesiosis vs leptospirosis
rationale: Post-mortem comparison with leptospirosis; no treatment described.

title: A unique case of Babesia gibsoni infected dog with paraplegia.
journal: Journal of parasitic diseases : official organ of the Indian Society for Parasitology
design: single case report of natural infection
rationale: One Rottweiler with paraplegia and laboratory abnormalities treated for 21 days, with complete clinical recovery.

title: Fatal Babesia canis canis infection in a splenectomized Estonian dog.
design: single fatal case report with two PCR-positive household dogs
rationale: Fatal case with supportive therapy only before euthanasia, plus a housemate treated with imidocarb that remained stable; outcome and treatment are described.

title: Plasma biomarkers of SIRS and MODS associated with canine babesiosis.
design: proteomic case-control study of admission plasma, four groups
rationale: Admission plasma proteomics by severity group; no treatment or outcome.

title: Therapeutic Effects of Atovaquone/Proguanil in Combination with Azithromycin in Dogs Naturally Infected with Babesia gibsoni
design: randomised two-arm treatment comparison, natural infection
rationale: Randomised two-arm comparison in 8 naturally infected puppies, with PCR clearance and haematocrit and platelet recovery reported.

title: Infectious diseases in dogs rescued during dogfighting investigations.
design: cross-sectional prevalence survey with PCV and anaemia association
rationale: Prevalence survey of seized dogs with anaemia association; no treatment or outcome.

design: case report of one bitch and her litter of three puppies
rationale: Bitch and three puppies treated with imidocarb, with improvement in 24-72 h and PCR-negative follow-up; aim is possible vertical transmission.

title: A review of canine babesiosis: the European perspective.
design: narrative review and practical guideline
species: B. canis, B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, B. vulpes
rationale: Practical guideline review covering diagnosis, treatment and prognosis of canine babesiosis in Europe.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging of Brain Involvement in Dogs Using Paramagnetic Contrast Enhancement with Mn(II)-DCTA P.

design: experimental contrast-enhanced MRI study in infected dogs
rationale: Contrast MRI of CNS lesions; no treatment of babesiosis described.

title: The prevalence of Dirofilaria repens in cats, healthy dogs and dogs with concurrent babesiosis in an expansion zone in central Europe.
design: survey plus comparison of B. canis dogs by D. repens co-infection
rationale: Co-infection prevalence and haematology; no treatment or outcome.

design: methodical guidelines (epizootiology, clinicopathology, drug efficacy)
rationale: Guidelines whose stated aims include treatment; they report clinicopathology of severe babesiosis and drug efficacy percentages (Babesan 96.5%, Forticarb 93.3% etc.) plus Emidonol shortening recovery and reducing complications. Sample size not reported, so n_dogs is null.

title: Spurious reticulocyte profiles in dogs with large form babesiosis: a retrospective study.
design: retrospective review of CBC reticulocyte dot plots
rationale: Retrospective review of CBC reticulocyte dot plots in dogs with babesiosis; no clinical presentation of treated dogs and no treatment or outcome reported.

rationale: Descriptive haematology of 101 positive dogs (anaemia, thrombocytopenia); abstract describes no treatment or outcome.
